verdict.tagline: Mindless cleaning satisfaction tempered by physical strain and stubborn dirt.
for_you_if: you find deep relaxation in methodical cleaning tasks
you want a podcast game for long sessions
you enjoy unlocking equipment upgrades over time
not_for_you_if: you suffer from motion sickness during camera movement
you experience hand cramps from continuous action
you rely on stable multiplayer netcode
you dislike hunting for tiny missed dirt spots

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players highlight severe multiplayer desync and frustrating dirt tracking issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report issues with multiplayer functionality, describing heavy lag or desync where the host falls behind other players.

citations.review_text:
multiplayer is broken, there's a massive delay for the host where the host will be 5-10 minutes behind everyone else you're playing with. this has been an issue with the game for over 3 years and still hasn't been fixed, do not buy if your intention is playing with friends.
product refunded.

Got this for multiplayer and its netcode is barely functional. Constant desyncs, name tags don't align with players, players getting kicked out mid-game and inability to load into servers.

Was looking forward to the core gameplay since I've worked as a pressure washer irl but refunding this out of principle of poor developer practices. Sequel's out and this game remains in an unfinished state, and the mountains of crossover dlc slop makes Paradox's games look consumer friendly when comparing the quality you get. I'd say get it on a discount but 4 years into release it still hasn't gone past 50%. Lacks soul and feels like an absolute cashgrab coasting on a lack of competition in the market.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe frustration with tracking down remaining dirt to finish cleaning jobs.

citations.review_text:
good game, unfortunately the Auto Complete feature makes it very annoying. I would not buy this or a sequel.
They should have some tech to check if that 10% is all bunched up together, or in different points of the object, and how far apart, and or have a scale to choose the auto complete threshold.
Additionally break big areas into smaller portions of that area, would make it less frustrating while not having this auto complete issue slap you in the face for being thorough.
BORING. Incredibly boring and it's also frustrating, its gonna say its 99% clean and done but you cant move on until you have checked every crevice, which is very time consuming. Not worth the price.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players note physical strain from continuous motions and difficulty finding hidden dirt spots.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that finding the final hidden spots of dirt or hard-to-reach areas can be difficult and frustrating.

citations.review_text:
Found this game from Markiplier, played it for 22 minutes at first and immediately fell in love. (ROFL) it's really fun if you just want smth mindless to keep you occupied.

Only dislike is some hard to reach places for dirt, or dirt that's practically invisible. I spent 10 minutes straight trying to finish cleaning the pond on the backyard because i couldn't find the hidden dirt spots (sobbing) 
And the birdhouse and grill in the same level, difficult to clean because of the hard to reach places.
And the dirtbike. Tiny places that are difficult to see.

But, it's still a really fun game!! 10/10 recommend
i like the game for the most part but sometimes when im finishing a section and the dirt is in a weird spot it can be hard to find and its just kinda annoying but other than that the game is good
i want to pressure wash myself everytime i have to find the last remaining speck of dirt that i missed

passes the time. good for podcasts. DLC hell. the most fun you'll have is chatting with your friend and occasionally spraying them. the least fun you'll have is cramming yourself into an odd angle to nip the last percent on a crevvvase.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the continuous cleaning motions cause physical strain such as wrist pain and hand cramps.

citations.review_text:
It's a good game. And somewhat relaxing. However, I feel like I'm shredding my wrist with the back and forth motions I'm constantly making to clean efficiently. I wish there were like macros you could record or preset repeatable move options so cleaning would be less taxing on my wrist.
It's a cool game. Would I use it to relax? Nah, not especially.

Very fun pass time game, just throw music on and time passes without you even realizing it. A lot of fun free levels and some paid ones if you are done with the main story but wanna keep playing. Only cons I've experienced is hand cramps (mostly my fault), buggy ladders and the useless soap nozzles. Other than that, this game is very addicting (might not be for some). If you do not like slower simulator games do not buy this, obviously.
This game enrages my carpal tunnel something fierce but it's so addicting. Stick a podcast on in the background and you're in for a hella relaxing time.
it hurts me physically but i love it

Is wish there was a mixed option for me to use.  I love this game; it's very soothing and therapeutic.  However, In the alter levels, the game started to lag and freeze up making it pretty much unplayable. claims.claim: Reviewers find certain small areas, corners, or remaining percentages of dirt extremely difficult to locate and clean.

citations.review_text:
There's alot more content than I was expecting in a game at this price. It took me around 50 hours to complete the campaign solo, and it's fun to play while listening to YouTube videos or something. 

I like the variety of levels, and how some of them are shorter and some are longer. How some are vehicles and how some are structures. 

[u]My only complaints:[/u]
- Some of the small pieces that you have to clean off are really hard to get to and complete, even with the orange highlighting effect.
- The specific material cleaners/soaps feel pretty useless, and are unsatisfying to use (I was expecting them to look foamy or something, not just... like the water you normally use).
>> Wish the material cleaners were also unlimited in stock, or just unlimited without having to buy them. There's only a limited stock of them for some reason.
- Wish more levels were unlocked at a time so you can come back to the one that you are "tired of" or have been working on for awhile later to get a change of scenery.
- I don't care about the texts you receive in this game. Let me work in peace.
- Not a fan of the art style of the game, but it launches, runs well, and there's plenty of content. Honestly all I can ask for at this point in games.
- Just a me-thing, but I wish there were more indoor levels. Those tended to be my favorites.

Other than that, if you like mindless tasks and want something to keep your hands and eyes busy, you should definitely give this game a try.

Chill game to clean off dirty properties / vehicles. The story is ridiculous, although cleaning glowy-things are fun. There are some fiddly bits to clean, even with the strongest available power washer, and it is tedious to clean high ceilings. 

If you get motion sickness playing this game, you'll want to increase the FOV in the Options and use turret mode (with C). That will help. 

Also somewhat annoying, but over half the achievements in this game come from completing DLC cleans.

Picked this up after having a blast (pun intended) pressure washing our patio irl and its probably one of my top 5 cosy games of all time. There is so much content and just enough customisation and tools to keep it fresh. Its so nice to sit down and pressure wash something while watching a tv show or listening to an audiobook on my phone, love a chill game like that.

Graphics are really nice, just “real” enough to not look cartoony.

Only gripe is it was a little buggy at times when you simply couldn’t see any dirt to wash off but still needed that 1%.

Rolled credits on the main career stuff and it was fantastic. So cosy and satisfying start to finish.

i remembered watching markiplier play this long ago and i can finally show my honest take!

I always thought that this is the ultimate "listen to a podcast or music" game which it makes it stress-relieving after a long day. However it can be a bit repetitive sometimes and it can be a drag to find last 1% of dirt hidden somewhere in a nook or cranny

8/10, Totally recommend you trying it! its my comfort game 🙂

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign as a lengthy timesink that can feel tedious or turn into a slog when played solo over a short period.

citations.review_text: Fun at first but gets monotonous, especially cleaning huge objects.  Campaign takes a long time if you are doing it solo.  I can see where the game would be more fun co-op.

The game is well-made.  The washing mechanics are relatively intuitive, the story going along in the background is fun to follow once it picks up, the upgrades feel decent to buy/see in-action, etc. The biggest problem for me is the timesink, though I think that has more to do with my personal preference than poor game design. I played through the entire game in 2 weeks and in hindsight this was a bad idea, as it turned what was supposed to be relaxing/calming into an absolute slog. By the 2nd half of the game I was just waiting for it to be over (even though I'd done this to myself), and when my progress accidentally reset back a few levels/jobs on one open of the game I uninstalled (luckily the next time I opened it it fixed itself somehow). 

The game is well-made and if you're interested I'd pick it up. You *have* to take it slow and not rush through the whole thing to enjoy it though. Great game for if you want something to do while watching a particular YouTube video, not a good game to grind out.

7/10.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Veterans enjoy career progression and co-op, while noting tedious hard-to-reach cleaning spots and downloadable content requirements.

claims.claim: The game allows players to purchase and play multiple DLC expansions containing additional jobs and achievements.

citations.review_text:
Great game for scratching that OCD itch.
However, after finishing the main story, only 40% of the achievements unlocked. Reaching 100% completion requires purchasing several DLCs. These expansions only offer about 5–6 jobs each, and almost all of them range from mediocre to meh.

Overall, a pleasant and satisfying experience! Definitely would recommend if you enjoyed the demo.

[h1] Positives [/h1]
[list]
[*]Watching progress of things being cleaned.
[*]Being able to ID and highlight areas that need to be cleaned.
[*]The little text messages that appear in each mission are enjoyable to read and gives the characters personalities despite no appearance of anyone beyond the player.
[*]An interesting story that I didn't expect the game to have.
[*]Achievements are pretty easy to get.
[*]The custom models of the player's gear and appearance for DLC missions are aesthetically pleasing.
[/list]

[h1] Negatives [/h1]
[list]
[*]You can't 100% this game's Achievements unless you buy the DLC, which is nearly $50 unless you wait for it to go on sale.
[*]The tower scaffolding is very inefficient and quite annoying to use as some placements are not allowed and if you fall, scaling it takes a while.
[*]Dirt and grime, especially in the DLCs, are sometimes placed in really narrow and difficult areas of objects.
[*]The highlight option via tablet is wildly unhelpful for some objects as it only pulses bright grey, which often made me overlook what I'm searching for. It doesn't help that small objects render this mechanic useless such as buttons and handles.
[/list]

It's a nice and relaxing game to play to pass the time or if you're just bored, there's a lot to do (clean) in this game and completing a task does feel like a somewhat true accomplishment.
While it certainly isn't for everyone, some people say it's boring which yeah after a while it can get a little tedious doing the same thing over and over for hours on end, it still is entertaining to just chill out and get a bunch of muck off of a house; car; or UFO! 
I like a lot of what this games offers, and I'm excited to see what other things the game will offer in the future!

Now my only real gripe with this game are the achievements.
With 100 achievements to get, you'd be surprised to find out that 60% of them are locked behind a paywall. Not just one, but MULTIPLE PAYWALLS! There's 6 DLCs that each include 10 achievements, and each one is around $10-15 CAD making it around $60-90 CAD with all of the DLCs bought.

Now I don't know about you, but I don't think ANY sort of achievement is worth 10 dollars, let alone nearly 100 dollars. I do like the base game achievements as they can add a challenge to your tasks that can be neat, but locking achievements behind a paywall where more than half of them are having you just completing the tasks the DLC comes with is pretty scummy and honestly makes getting the DLCs to 100% the game less worth it :/

But that's my only real issue with this game everything else is great. I love the calming nature of the game, I enjoy the look & style of the game, and I hope the devs do something about the DLC achievements eventually :]

claims.claim: Cleaning hard-to-reach areas, small details, and high irregular surfaces can be tedious, requiring awkward positioning or precise mouse movements.

citations.review_text:
PowerWash Simulator turns the mundane act of removing grime into a meditative process that rewards patience with immediate visual transformation. Stripping layers of dirt from complex machinery using high-pressure water creates an oddly cathartic rhythm that keeps the player focused on the steady progress of restoring ruined surfaces to beauty.

Upgrading from the starter equipment to professional power washers, nozzles, and various extensions provides a tangible sense of accomplishment during career mode. These mechanical improvements feel essential as the jobs grow increasingly intricate, allowing one to approach larger cleaning challenges with greater efficiency rather than becoming bogged down by tediousness.

Venturing through the massive volume of available content, including licensed expansions like the Final Fantasy 7 and Tomb Raider packs, significantly bolsters the overall value. Each level captures a distinct personality through humorous text messages from town residents, adding a layer of charm that keeps the atmosphere grounded and engaging.

Navigating fiddly, small-part-heavy objects requires precision that sometimes highlights the limitations of using a controller over a mouse. While a gamepad remains comfortable for long sessions, cleaning the final remaining spots on complex geometry often necessitates switching inputs or adopting a two-pass strategy to ensure total surface coverage.

Hunting for the final one per cent of dirt can occasionally shift the tone from relaxing to slightly taxing during brighter stages. Although the highlight feature proves helpful, the persistent search for tiny missed spots might temporarily break the zen-like state established by the otherwise satisfying audio and visual feedback loop.

Achievement challenges such as time trials or water-usage limitations offer a frantic diversion that contrasts sharply with the standard meditative pace. These optional objectives introduce a layer of stress that feels entirely separat…

Overall, a pleasant and satisfying experience! Definitely would recommend if you enjoyed the demo.

[h1] Positives [/h1]
[list]
[*]Watching progress of things being cleaned.
[*]Being able to ID and highlight areas that need to be cleaned.
[*]The little text messages that appear in each mission are enjoyable to read and gives the characters personalities despite no appearance of anyone beyond the player.
[*]An interesting story that I didn't expect the game to have.
[*]Achievements are pretty easy to get.
[*]The custom models of the player's gear and appearance for DLC missions are aesthetically pleasing.
[/list]

[h1] Negatives [/h1]
[list]
[*]You can't 100% this game's Achievements unless you buy the DLC, which is nearly $50 unless you wait for it to go on sale.
[*]The tower scaffolding is very inefficient and quite annoying to use as some placements are not allowed and if you fall, scaling it takes a while.
[*]Dirt and grime, especially in the DLCs, are sometimes placed in really narrow and difficult areas of objects.
[*]The highlight option via tablet is wildly unhelpful for some objects as it only pulses bright grey, which often made me overlook what I'm searching for. It doesn't help that small objects render this mechanic useless such as buttons and handles.
[/list]

PowerWash Simulator places you in the role of the sole owner and operator of a pressure washing business. Outfitted with an upgradeable pressure washer, a wand connected to a hose that blasts water with incredible force, you guide the player character through dozens of job sites, cleaning up layers of dirt, grime, oil, and mold from vehicles, buildings, and entire stretches of property for an array of wacky customers. Jobs vary in size. Some may be completed in minutes. The largest can take more than five hours to finish in their entirety. As boring and absurd as this premise may seem, I find it to be a fulfilling experience that clarifies and reinforces why I love videogames.

PowerWash Simulator has one of the simplest premises of any videogame I have ever described. From a first-person perspective and using typical first-person shooting controls, point the player character’s pressure washer at something dirty and blast it with water until it is clean. The challenge, if it can be called that, is the scale and intricacy of the property they are charged with cleaning. Every centimeter of their current job is caked with some kind of filth. On the largest levels, the difficulty comes from cleaning vast surfaces, often including the walls, floors, and ceilings of entire buildings. For the smaller, vehicle-focused levels, the difficulty comes from all the tiny nooks and crevices that make up their decorations and machinery, requiring each component to be cleaned from every possible angle.

Many features of the interface are of great help in completing the player character’s jobs. A gauge in the top-left corner shows the current percentage of dirt that has been cleaned. Every twenty percent cleaned earns a star towards the job completion rating. It’s not necessary to earn all five stars on every job as new ones generally unlock every few stars. If I do decide to carry on to complete a one hundred percent clean job—and I always do—additional tools make the task easier…

I know I got 100+ hours on this thing but tbh I played it all in a frenzied state over the course of two weeks or so and now just looking at it churns my stomach a little bit. This game has very little in it to enjoy, seeing the clean surfaces underneath the dirt is satisfying but the actual way you get that done is the most ass possible. There are so many times here where what you need to clean is a high irregular surface that cannot be easily hit with your power washer and you're going to spend a lot of time trying to hover your mouse over minute little centimeters of space on a pipe or handle or whatever, and that's assuming these places are even accessible, because oftentimes surfaces will be literally beyond your reach and neither the extender nor the scaffold will be enough to reach them without some weird, infuriating amount of contortionism or parkouring on your part. It completely voids any claim this game has of being relaxing. A lot of it is presumably supposed to be easier to do if you use the cleaning product setting, except the cleaning products last so little that in the early game, when you need to save for better power washers, they feel like a waste of money, and then in the later game, when you already have all power washers, they make so little difference they feel completely superfluous. It's also, minus DLC, way too short for its full asking price, considering how banal of a gameplay loop it has to offer. TL;DR its not polished enough to be relaxing and it's too simplistic to be engaging. There's clearly better options in matter of cleaning games.

claims.claim: Co-op multiplayer is included, allowing players to team up with friends to clean levels together.

citations.review_text:
Powerwash Simulator is an amazing cleaning game. The controls and mechanics are simple, meaning it’s a nice cosy game you can put on in the background of doing other task, such as talking to friends in call, listening to an audiobook or is great for playing with friends in co-op. I originally purchased the game to play with friends, and really enjoyed it, and came back to it a year later to 100% it on my own, as most of my friends had finished the game at this point, hence why I said this game is enjoyable both solo and with friends.

Out of all the DLC’s, I think the Wallace and Gromit one was my favourite, but I think all the DLC’s for this game were quite good.

Overall, an amazing game, and would highly recommend.

The perfect game for just chill, no consequences, easy, and SATISFYING gameplay. You can take it as easy or as serious as you want. With mountains of extra FREE content, and even more in paid DLC, you can easily put in 100+ hours into this game while just chilling/vibing to anything anything (movies, youtube, music, whatever). I can't think of a better game in this category. Many maps/levels are absolutely gorgeous too, especially after cleaning them up!

Power wash simulator is a cleaning game where you can have up to 4 players cleaning multiple levels to make it all shine,

The game has great DLC, which you can play with friends or with the wife and have a washie fight.

You can buy new equipment's for your washie, and outfits that are out of this world.

i did enjoy this game, and will be buying powerwash 2 soon.

The levels are very well done.

The graphics are great especially Back to the future DLC.

I would have loved a Halo level where you can clean the warthog, or the pelican, or better The library level.

The sound can sometimes be choppy or no audio at all.

If your into a relaxing game, or just to waste time then this game is for you.

As for the price, I'd suggest buying on a sale.

I recommend this game.

8/10

Super Relaxing and Surprisingly Addictive

PowerWash Simulator is one of those games you don’t expect much from at first, but once you start playing, it’s incredibly hard to put down. It’s super relaxing, chill, and honestly one of the most satisfying games I’ve played in a while.

There’s something about watching all the dirt and grime disappear that just hits different. It’s very calming and almost therapeutic, especially after a long day. You can just sit back, take your time, and enjoy the process without any stress.

What makes it even better is playing with friends. Cleaning together, messing around, and just vibing while getting things done makes the experience even more fun. It turns a simple concept into something really enjoyable and memorable.

The progression system keeps things interesting, and each new job feels rewarding. It’s simple, but that’s what makes it so good. No pressure, no rush, just pure satisfaction.

If you’re looking for a game to unwind, relax, or just have a good time with friends, I highly recommend this.

10/10 – way more fun than it sounds.

Navigating fiddly, small-part-heavy objects requires precision that sometimes highlights the limitations of using a controller over a mouse. While a gamepad remains comfortable for long sessions, cleaning the final remaining spots on complex geometry often necessitates switching inputs or adopting a two-pass strategy to ensure total surface coverage.

Hunting for the final one per cent of dirt can occasionally shift the tone from relaxing to slightly taxing during brighter stages. Although the highlight feature proves helpful, the persistent search for tiny missed spots might temporarily break the zen-like state established by the otherwise satisfying audio and visual feedback loop.

Achievement challenges such as time trials or water-usage limitations offer a frantic diversion that contrasts sharply with the standard meditative pace. These optional objectives introduce a layer of stress that feels entirely separat…

PowerWash Simulator places you in the role of the sole owner and operator of a pressure washing business. Outfitted with an upgradeable pressure washer, a wand connected to a hose that blasts water with incredible force, you guide the player character through dozens of job sites, cleaning up layers of dirt, grime, oil, and mold from vehicles, buildings, and entire stretches of property for an array of wacky customers. Jobs vary in size. Some may be completed in minutes. The largest can take more than five hours to finish in their entirety. As boring and absurd as this premise may seem, I find it to be a fulfilling experience that clarifies and reinforces why I love videogames.

PowerWash Simulator has one of the simplest premises of any videogame I have ever described. From a first-person perspective and using typical first-person shooting controls, point the player character’s pressure washer at something dirty and blast it with water until it is clean. The challenge, if it can be called that, is the scale and intricacy of the property they are charged with cleaning. Every centimeter of their current job is caked with some kind of filth. On the largest levels, the difficulty comes from cleaning vast surfaces, often including the walls, floors, and ceilings of entire buildings. For the smaller, vehicle-focused levels, the difficulty comes from all the tiny nooks and crevices that make up their decorations and machinery, requiring each component to be cleaned from every possible angle.

Many features of the interface are of great help in completing the player character’s jobs. A gauge in the top-left corner shows the current percentage of dirt that has been cleaned. Every twenty percent cleaned earns a star towards the job completion rating. It’s not necessary to earn all five stars on every job as new ones generally unlock every few stars. If I do decide to carry on to complete a one hundred percent clean job—and I always do—additional tools make the task easier…

Power wash simulator is a cleaning game where you can have up to 4 players cleaning multiple levels to make it all shine,

The game has great DLC, which you can play with friends or with the wife and have a washie fight.

You can buy new equipment's for your washie, and outfits that are out of this world.

i did enjoy this game, and will be buying powerwash 2 soon.

The levels are very well done.

The graphics are great especially Back to the future DLC.

I would have loved a Halo level where you can clean the warthog, or the pelican, or better The library level.

The sound can sometimes be choppy or no audio at all.

If your into a relaxing game, or just to waste time then this game is for you.

As for the price, I'd suggest buying on a sale.

I recommend this game.

8/10

citations.review_text:
Overall, a pleasant and satisfying experience! Definitely would recommend if you enjoyed the demo.

[h1] Positives [/h1]
[list]
[*]Watching progress of things being cleaned.
[*]Being able to ID and highlight areas that need to be cleaned.
[*]The little text messages that appear in each mission are enjoyable to read and gives the characters personalities despite no appearance of anyone beyond the player.
[*]An interesting story that I didn't expect the game to have.
[*]Achievements are pretty easy to get.
[*]The custom models of the player's gear and appearance for DLC missions are aesthetically pleasing.
[/list]

[h1] Negatives [/h1]
[list]
[*]You can't 100% this game's Achievements unless you buy the DLC, which is nearly $50 unless you wait for it to go on sale.
[*]The tower scaffolding is very inefficient and quite annoying to use as some placements are not allowed and if you fall, scaling it takes a while.
[*]Dirt and grime, especially in the DLCs, are sometimes placed in really narrow and difficult areas of objects.
[*]The highlight option via tablet is wildly unhelpful for some objects as it only pulses bright grey, which often made me overlook what I'm searching for. It doesn't help that small objects render this mechanic useless such as buttons and handles.
[/list]

It's a nice and relaxing game to play to pass the time or if you're just bored, there's a lot to do (clean) in this game and completing a task does feel like a somewhat true accomplishment.
While it certainly isn't for everyone, some people say it's boring which yeah after a while it can get a little tedious doing the same thing over and over for hours on end, it still is entertaining to just chill out and get a bunch of muck off of a house; car; or UFO! 
I like a lot of what this games offers, and I'm excited to see what other things the game will offer in the future!

Now my only real gripe with this game are the achievements.
With 100 achievements to get, you'd be surprised to find out that 60% of them are locked behind a paywall. Not just one, but MULTIPLE PAYWALLS! There's 6 DLCs that each include 10 achievements, and each one is around $10-15 CAD making it around $60-90 CAD with all of the DLCs bought.

Now I don't know about you, but I don't think ANY sort of achievement is worth 10 dollars, let alone nearly 100 dollars. I do like the base game achievements as they can add a challenge to your tasks that can be neat, but locking achievements behind a paywall where more than half of them are having you just completing the tasks the DLC comes with is pretty scummy and honestly makes getting the DLCs to 100% the game less worth it :/

But that's my only real issue with this game everything else is great. I love the calming nature of the game, I enjoy the look & style of the game, and I hope the devs do something about the DLC achievements eventually :]

[h1][u]Aspects[/u][/h1]

[b]Multiplayer - Relaxing - Sandbox - Funny[/b]

[b][u]Rating:[/u] 9.5/10[/b]

[b][u]Replay value:[/u] Yes[/b]


[h1][u]Thoughts[/u][/h1]

For a relaxation/sandbox game, this is easily one of my favorite games of all time. It's insanely satisfying to clean through all the maps they provide, and lawd do they provide content. I have 100+ hours of game time, and that involved the main story, challenge modes, DLC, and co-op runs. Completion satisfaction in this game is great, and it's perfect for playing while watching something or talking to friends. You get customization throughout the game, and you also come across mini easter eggs from time to time. My only complaint about this game is having to buy the DLC's to 100% it, but aside from that it's incredible. BUYYYYY
